questions.question: What is the Rigvedic name of the river Ravi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parushni**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Parushni is the Rigvedic name of the river Ravi**.

 
 
• The Ravi was known as **Purushni or Iravati** to Indians in Vedic times and as Hydraotes to the Ancient Greeks.
 
• The Rig-Veda civilization was **centred on the River Saraswati **which is now lost** in the Deserts of Rajasthan.**
 
• The Ravi River, a transboundary river of India and Pakistan, is an integral part of the Indus River Basin and forms the headwaters of the Indus basin.
 
 
• **It rises in the Himalayas in Himachal Pradesh state,** India, and** flows west-northwest past Chamba,** turning southwest at the boundary of Jammu and Kashmir state.
 
 
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

• Vedic texts have a wide geographical horizon, speaking of oceans, rivers, mountains and deserts.
 
• The Vedic land is a land of **seven rivers** flowing into the ocean.
 
• **Central Rivers (rivers of Punjab):**
 
 
• Vitasta (Jhelum)
 
• Asikni (Chenab)
 
• Parusni (Ravi)
 
• Vipas (Beas)

questions.question: Buddha meditated for days on end under a peepal tree at ______, where he attained enlightenment.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bodh Gaya.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bodh Gaya** is a small town in the state of **Bihar, India**, and it is **one of the most sacred sites in Buddhism.**
 
• It was at Bodh Gaya, **under a peepal tree** known as the **Bodhi Tree**, that Siddhartha Gautama, later known as Buddha, **attained enlightenment.**
 
• The site of Bodh Gaya is **marked by the Mahabodhi Temple**, which is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site **and an important pilgrimage destination for Buddhists worldwide.
 
• The temple complex houses the** sacred Bodhi Tree,** **the Vajrasana (Diamond Throne)** where Buddha meditated, and various other monastic structures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sarnath:**

 
 
• Sarnath, located near** Varanasi **in Uttar Pradesh, is where** Buddha delivered his first sermon **after attaining enlightenment.
 
• It is a significant pilgrimage site for Buddhists.
 
 
 
• **Kushinagar: **
 
 
• Kushinagar, also in Uttar Pradesh, is the place where **Buddha attained Mahaparinirvana (passed away)**.
 
• It is an important Buddhist pilgrimage site and has several **monastic ruins and stupas.**
 
 
 
• **Ujjain: **
 
 
• Ujjain is an ancient city in **Madhya Pradesh **and holds** religious importance in Hinduism.**
 
• It is associated with the** Kumbh Mela **and is known for its ancient temples, but it is not directly linked to Buddha's life or enlightenment.

questions.question: How many Vedangas are there in total?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Six**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Six Vedangas are there in total. **

 
 
• The Vedanga are **six auxiliary disciplines of Hinduism that developed in ancient times** and have been connected with the study of the Vedas.
 
• They are as follows:
 
 
• Shiksha (Phonetics)
 
• Kalpa (Ritual Canon)
 
• Vyakaran (Grammar)
 
• Nirukta (explanation)
 
• Chhanda (Vedic meter)
 
• Jyotisha (Astrology)
 
 
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Shiksha :**

 
 
• This auxiliary discipline has focused on the letters of the** Sanskrit alphabet, accent, quantity, stress, melody, and rules of euphonic combination of words during a Vedic recitation.**
 
 
 
• **Chandas :**
 
 
• This auxiliary discipline has focused on the** poetic meters, including those based on a fixed number of syllables per verse, and those based on a fixed number of morae perverse.**
 
 
 
• **Vyakarana :**
 
 
• This auxiliary discipline has focused on the** rules of grammar and linguistic analysis to establish the exact form of words and sentences to properly express ideas.**
 
 
 
• **Nirukta :**
 
 
• This auxiliary discipline has focused on **linguistic analysis to help establish the proper meaning of the words, given the context they are used in**.
 
 
 
• **Kalpa :**
 
 
• This field focused on** standardizing procedures for Vedic rituals, rites of passage rituals associated with major life events such as a birth, wedding, and death in the family, **as well as discussing the personal conduct and proper duties of an individual in different stages of his life.
 
 
 
• **Jyotisha :**
 
 
• This auxiliary Vedic discipline focuse**d on time keeping.**

questions.question: The founder of the Pallava dynasty was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Simhavishnu**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Simhavishnu** was the founder of the **Pallava dynasty**.
 
• The Pallava dynasty was a Tamil dynasty that ruled parts of South India from the 3rd century to the 9th century.
 
• Simhavishnu's reign marked the rise of the Pallavas to prominence in the region.
 
• The Pallavas are known for their patronage of architecture, particularly the rock-cut temples of Mahabalipuram.
 
• The dynasty played a crucial role in the cultural and political history of South India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Pallavas were instrumental in the development of **Dravidian architecture**.
 
• Their rule saw the construction of several notable temples, including the **Shore Temple and the Pancha Rathas at Mahabalipuram**.
 
• Simhavishnu's successors, such as Mahendravarman I and Narasimhavarman I, continued to expand the dynasty's influence and patronage of the arts.
 
• The Pallavas had a significant impact on the cultural and religious landscape of South India, with contributions to both Hinduism and Buddhism.

questions.question: The famous Chinese traveller Hieun Tsang visited India during which Emperor's reign?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harshavardhana.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• During the reign of **Harshavardhana** famous Chinese traveler,** Hieun Tsang** visited India.
 
• The Chinese traveler,** Hiuen Tsang**, who visited India during his reign, has given a vivid description of the social, economic, and religious conditions, under the rule of **Harsha **spoke highly of the king.
 
• **Harshavardhana** is well known for his religious toleration, able administration, and diplomatic relations. He maintained diplomatic relations with China and sent envoys, who exchanged ideas of the Chinese rulers and developed their knowledge about each other.
 
• **In 620 A.D**. Harshavardhana invaded the **Chalukya kingdom **in the Deccan, which was then ruled by** Pulakesin II**. But the Chalukya resistance proved tough for Harshavardhana and he was defeated.
 
• **Hiuen Tsang** has taught many secrets of **Chinese wisdom to Indians**. Hiuen Tsang returned to China he brought with him Sanskrit scriptures and books of wisdom.

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of ‘Vikramshila Vishwavidyalaya’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dharmapala**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vikramshila Vishwavidyalaya** was founded by **Dharmapala**, a ruler of the Pala dynasty in ancient India.
 
• Dharmapala was a significant patron of Buddhism and established Vikramshila as a major center of Buddhist learning in the late 8th or early 9th century.
 
• The university was renowned for its specialized training in Buddhist teachings, particularly the Vajrayana tradition.
 
• Vikramshila was one of the two most important centers of Buddhist learning in India during its time, the other being Nalanda.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dharmapala** ruled during the 8th century and was a key figure in the establishment of several educational institutions in ancient India.
 
• Under his reign, the Pala dynasty saw a cultural and educational renaissance, with significant contributions to art, architecture, and learning.
 
• The ruins of Vikramshila University are located in the Bhagalpur district of Bihar, India.
 
• Vikramshila University was destroyed during the invasions of Bakhtiyar Khilji in the late 12th century, similar to the fate of Nalanda University.

questions.question: Which power were the Badami (or Vatapi) Chalukyas originally subjects of?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kadambas**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kadambas** were the original power to whom the **Badami (or Vatapi) Chalukyas** were subjects.
 
• The Kadambas ruled from Banavasi in present-day Karnataka, and their reign is considered significant in the early medieval history of the Deccan region.
 
• The Chalukyas later rose to prominence and established their own dynasty, with Badami (Vatapi) as their capital.
 
• The Chalukyas are well-known for their contributions to art and architecture, particularly in the construction of rock-cut temples.
 
• The transition from being subjects of the Kadambas to establishing their own rule marks a significant period in South Indian history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Badami Chalukyas** ruled from the** 6th to the 8th century CE** and are known for their architectural innovations and military prowess.
 
• Their capital, Badami, is famous for its cave temples, which are exemplary specimens of Indian rock-cut architecture.
 
• The Chalukyas fought several wars with neighboring dynasties such as the **Pallavas and the Rashtrakutas**, which shaped the political landscape of the region.
 
• The Kadambas, on the other hand, are one of the earliest native dynasties to rule over Karnataka and are credited with laying the foundation for the later development of Kannada literature and culture.
 
• The period of **Chalukya rule** is often regarded as a g**olden age in the history of Karnataka**, characterized by economic prosperity and cultural achievements.

questions.question: Prabhavati Gupta, the Queen Regent of the Vakataka empire, was the daughter of Kuberanaga and ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prabhavati Gupta was the daughter of Chandragupta II and her mother was Kuberanaga, of the Naga.**

 
 
• One of the most important rulers in early Indian history.
 
• She was married to Rudrasena II of the Vakataka Dynasty.
 
 
• After his death in 390, she ruled as regent for her two young sons, Divakarasena and Damodarasena for twenty years with the help of her father.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Chandragupta II ascended the throne after Ramgupta and assumed the title 'Vikramaditya'. **
 
 
• He was a patron of art and literature since his court was adorned with Navaratnas including Kalidasa, the Shakespeare of India. 
 
• He was the first Gupta ruler to have issued silver coins. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **​Chandragupta II :**

 
 
• He is also known by his title Vikramaditya was one of the most powerful emperors of the Gupta Empire in northern India.
 
• The Gupta empire reached its zenith during the rule of Chandragupta.
 
• The legendary figure of Vikramaditya is probably based on Chandragupta II (among other kings), and the noted Sanskrit poet Kalidasa may have been his court poet.
 
 
 
• **The Gupta Empire :**
 
 
• The Gupta Empire was an ancient Indian empire that existed from the early 4th century CE to the late 6th century CE.
 
• At its zenith, from approximately 319 to 467 CE, it covered much of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• **This period is considered the Golden Age of India by historians.**
 
• The ruling dynasty of the empire was founded by the king Sri Gupta; the most notable rulers of the dynasty were Chandragupta I, Samudragupta, and Chandragupta II alias Vikramaditya.

questions.question: Which of the following name was used for the Indian subcontinent by ancient travellers like Megasthenes, FaHien, Huen Tsang, Al Beruni, Ibn Batuta etc. for the active contribution of Indian traders?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swaran Bhoomi.**____** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Swaran Bhoomi**

 
 
• **'Swaran Bhoomi'** was used for the Indian subcontinent by ancient travellers like** Megasthenes, FaHien, Huen Tsang, Al Beruni, Ibn Batuta etc.**
 
• Between the first to seventh centuries, India was the largest economy of the ancient and Medieval World.
 
• Approximately** one-third to one-fourth** **of the world's wealth** is under their control.
 
• In the writings of several travelers, the country was referred to as** Swaranbhumi and Swaran deep.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Suvarnabhumi **appears in many ancient Indian literary sources and Buddhist texts.
 
• Suvarnabhumi means **"Golden Land".**
 
• Ancient sources have associated it with one of a variety of places throughout the Southeast Asia region.
 
• There were texts mentioning Suvarnabhumi as a land of fortune where an Ancient Prince's ship was boarded for trade.
 
• Suvarnabhumi is known to be a land of richness and abundance.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Pala Dynasty of eastern India is INCORRECT?

options.text: Devapala was the grandson of Gopala.
The Pala kings were the followers of Buddhism.
The Pala dynasty was founded by Gopala.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dharmapala founded the Valabhi university**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dharmapala founded the Vikramashila University**, not the Valabhi university.
 
• The Pala Dynasty was an important ruling dynasty in eastern India, particularly in the regions of Bengal and Bihar.
 
• Devapala, the third ruler of the Pala Dynasty, was indeed the grandson of Gopala, the dynasty's founder.
 
• The Pala kings were notable patrons of Buddhism and played a significant role in the spread of Mahayana Buddhism in Tibet.
 
• Gopala, who founded the Pala dynasty, came to power around the mid-8th century CE.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Pala Dynasty is known for its contributions to the art, culture, and architecture of Bengal and Bihar regions.
 
• The dynasty's name "Pala" means "protector" and was used as a suffix to the names of all Pala monarchs.
 
• Dharmapala, one of the most prominent rulers of the Pala Dynasty, was instrumental in establishing the Pala influence over northern India.
 
• The Pala period is often regarded as a high point in the history of Bengal and Bihar, marked by prosperity and cultural flourishing.
 
• The Pala rulers were also known for their military prowess and diplomatic relations with other regional powers.

• ** Excavations of the site between 1990 and 2005 under the supervision of archaeologist R S Bisht** revealed the ancient city, which was a commercial and manufacturing centre for about 1,500 years before its collapse and eventual ruin in 1500 BC.

questions.question: Meghaduta was written by which poet of ancient India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalidasa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Kalidasa wrote two khandakavyas (minor poems):

 
 
• Ṛitusaṃhara describes the six seasons by narrating the experiences of two lovers in each of the seasons.
 
• Meghaduta (The Cloud Messenger), is the story of a Yaksha trying to send a message to his lover through a cloud.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kalidasa also wrote three plays:

 
 
• Malavikagnimitram (Pertaining to Malavika and Agnimitra) tells the story of King Agnimitra, who falls in love with the picture of an exiled servant girl named Malavika. 
 
• Abhijnanasakuntalam (Of the recollection of Shakuntala) tells the story of King Dushyanta who, while on a hunting trip, meets Shakuntala, **the adopted daughter of a sage, and marries her.**
 
• Vikramorvasiyam (Urvashi Won by Valour) tells the story of mortal King Pururavas and celestial nymph Urvashi who fall in love. 
 
 
 
• Kalidasa is also the author of two epic poems:
 
 
• Raghuvaṃsa is an epic poem about the kings of the **Raghu dynasty.**
 
• Kumarasambhava describes the birth and adolescence of the goddess Parvati, and her marriage with** Lord Shiva.**

questions.question: Inscriptions composed in praise of kings of ancient India are known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Prashastis.**__

__
 
• **Prashastis** is a special **kind of inscription, meaning “in praise of”. **They were composed by learned **Brahmans in praise of the rulers.**
 
• They tell us how rulers of that time wanted to** illustrate themselves.**
 
• If the kings liked the **prashastis,** they gave **land as a gift to the Brahmans,** with records of it on **copper plates.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
 

 **Tripitakas**
 Tripiṭaka or Tipiṭaka is the traditional term for the Buddhist scriptures
 
 

 **Sutras**
 Sutras are a genre of ancient and medieval Indian texts found in Hinduism, Buddhism and Jainism.
 
 

 **Jatakas**
 The Jataka tales are a voluminous body of literature native to India concerning the previous births of Gautama Buddha in both human and animal form

questions.question: Which was the first empire in ancient India to use elephants in its war on a large scale?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Magadha.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The first empire in ancient India to use elephants in its war on a large scale is **Magadha.**
 
• The evidence proved that the war elephant was invented in the **later Vedic period.**
 
• The interstate warfare under the process of unification of the kingdom **Magadha.**
 
• Magadha's success in unifying northern India's warring states is dependent on the** success of the elephant war.**

questions.question: Which of the following sites of Indus valley civilization is not on the bank of river Indus ?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is - __Ropar__**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Ropar__**

 __
 
• Located in present-day Punjab on the banks of the **Sutlej River__**, not the Indus.
 
• Excavated by **__Y.D. Sharma__**; one of the few Harappan sites in the easternmost region.
 
• Shows evidence of **__Harappan to post-Harappan cultural sequence__**.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__ **

__
 
• **Mohenjodaro__**

 __
 
• Situated on the **right bank of the Indus River__**.
 
• Known for the **__Great Bath__** and advanced drainage system.
 
 
 
• **__Chanhudaro__**
 __
 
• Located in Sindh, near the **Indus basin__**.
 
• Famous as a centre for **__bead making__**.
 
 
 
• **__Kot Diji__**
 __
 
• Situated on the **left bank of the Indus__** in Sindh.
 
• Represents the **__Kot Diji pre-Harappan phase__** preceding mature Harappan culture.
